nodes.Name: State
nodes.DocComment:
State represents the printer state passed to custom formatters.
It provides access to the [io.Writer] interface plus information about
the flags and options for the operand's format specifier.

nodes.Name: Formatter
nodes.DocComment:
Formatter is implemented by any value that has a Format method.
The implementation controls how [State] and rune are interpreted,
and may call [Sprint] or [Fprint](f) etc. to generate its output.

nodes.Name: Stringer
nodes.DocComment:
Stringer is implemented by any value that has a String method,
which defines the “native” format for that value.
The String method is used to print values passed as an operand
to any format that accepts a string or to an unformatted printer
such as [Print].

nodes.Name: GoStringer
nodes.DocComment:
GoStringer is implemented by any value that has a GoString method,
which defines the Go syntax for that value.
The GoString method is used to print values passed as an operand
to a %#v format.

nodes.Name: FormatString
nodes.DocComment:
FormatString returns a string representing the fully qualified formatting
directive captured by the [State], followed by the argument verb. ([State] does not
itself contain the verb.) The result has a leading percent sign followed by any
flags, the width, and the precision. Missing flags, width, and precision are
omitted. This function allows a [Formatter] to reconstruct the original
directive triggering the call to Format.

nodes.Name: buffer
nodes.DocComment: Use simple []byte instead of bytes.Buffer to avoid large dependency.

nodes.Name: pp
nodes.DocComment: pp is used to store a printer's state and is reused with sync.Pool to avoid allocations.

nodes.Name: newPrinter
nodes.DocComment: newPrinter allocates a new pp struct or grabs a cached one.

nodes.Name: free
nodes.DocComment: free saves used pp structs in ppFree; avoids an allocation per invocation.

nodes.Name: Write
nodes.DocComment:
Write implements [io.Writer] so we can call [Fprintf] on a pp (through [State]), for
recursive use in custom verbs.

nodes.Name: WriteString
nodes.DocComment:
WriteString implements [io.StringWriter] so that we can call [io.WriteString]
on a pp (through state), for efficiency.

nodes.Name: Fprintf
nodes.DocComment:
Fprintf formats according to a format specifier and writes to w.
It returns the number of bytes written and any write error encountered.

nodes.Name: Printf
nodes.DocComment:
Printf formats according to a format specifier and writes to standard output.
It returns the number of bytes written and any write error encountered.

nodes.Name: Sprintf
nodes.DocComment: Sprintf formats according to a format specifier and returns the resulting string.

nodes.Name: Appendf
nodes.DocComment:
Appendf formats according to a format specifier, appends the result to the byte
slice, and returns the updated slice.

nodes.Name: Fprint
nodes.DocComment:
Fprint formats using the default formats for its operands and writes to w.
Spaces are added between operands when neither is a string.
It returns the number of bytes written and any write error encountered.

nodes.Name: Print
nodes.DocComment:
Print formats using the default formats for its operands and writes to standard output.
Spaces are added between operands when neither is a string.
It returns the number of bytes written and any write error encountered.

nodes.Name: Sprint
nodes.DocComment:
Sprint formats using the default formats for its operands and returns the resulting string.
Spaces are added between operands when neither is a string.

nodes.Name: Append
nodes.DocComment:
Append formats using the default formats for its operands, appends the result to
the byte slice, and returns the updated slice.

nodes.Name: Fprintln
nodes.DocComment:
Fprintln formats using the default formats for its operands and writes to w.
Spaces are always added between operands and a newline is appended.
It returns the number of bytes written and any write error encountered.

nodes.Name: Println
nodes.DocComment:
Println formats using the default formats for its operands and writes to standard output.
Spaces are always added between operands and a newline is appended.
It returns the number of bytes written and any write error encountered.

nodes.Name: Sprintln
nodes.DocComment:
Sprintln formats using the default formats for its operands and returns the resulting string.
Spaces are always added between operands and a newline is appended.

nodes.Name: Appendln
nodes.DocComment:
Appendln formats using the default formats for its operands, appends the result
to the byte slice, and returns the updated slice. Spaces are always added
between operands and a newline is appended.

nodes.Name: getField
nodes.DocComment:
getField gets the i'th field of the struct value.
If the field itself is a non-nil interface, return a value for
the thing inside the interface, not the interface itself.

nodes.Name: tooLarge
nodes.DocComment:
tooLarge reports whether the magnitude of the integer is
too large to be used as a formatting width or precision.

nodes.Name: parsenum
nodes.DocComment: parsenum converts ASCII to integer.  num is 0 (and isnum is false) if no number present.

nodes.Name: fmt0x64
nodes.DocComment:
fmt0x64 formats a uint64 in hexadecimal and prefixes it with 0x or
not, as requested, by temporarily setting the sharp flag.

nodes.Name: fmtInteger
nodes.DocComment: fmtInteger formats a signed or unsigned integer.

nodes.Name: fmtFloat
nodes.DocComment:
fmtFloat formats a float. The default precision for each verb
is specified as last argument in the call to fmt_float.

nodes.Name: fmtComplex
nodes.DocComment:
fmtComplex formats a complex number v with
r = real(v) and j = imag(v) as (r+ji) using
fmtFloat for r and j formatting.

nodes.Name: printValue
nodes.DocComment:
printValue is similar to printArg but starts with a reflect value, not an interface{} value.
It does not handle 'p' and 'T' verbs because these should have been already handled by printArg.

nodes.Name: intFromArg
nodes.DocComment: intFromArg gets the argNumth element of a. On return, isInt reports whether the argument has integer type.

Children.Name: case
Children.RawSource: reflect.Uint, reflect.Uint8, reflect.Uint16, reflect.Uint32, reflect.Uint64, reflect.Uintptr

nodes.Name: parseArgNumber
nodes.DocComment:
parseArgNumber returns the value of the bracketed number, minus 1
(explicit argument numbers are one-indexed but we want zero-indexed).
The opening bracket is known to be present at format[0].
The returned values are the index, the number of bytes to consume
up to the closing paren, if present, and whether the number parsed
ok. The bytes to consume will be 1 if no closing paren is present.

nodes.Name: argNumber
nodes.DocComment:
argNumber returns the next argument to evaluate, which is either the value of the passed-in
argNum or the value of the bracketed integer that begins format[i:]. It also returns
the new value of i, that is, the index of the next byte of the format to process.

nodes.Name: doPrintln
nodes.DocComment:
doPrintln is like doPrint but always adds a space between arguments
and a newline after the last argument.
